precepts.text: The temple had money for widows, so why did the Grecians murmur that their widows were neglected? Because these were followers of Christ, and the priesthood had already agreed to cast out any man who confessed him. So the twelve said, look ye out among you seven men of honest report, full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom. Serving tables means taking care of the widows and orphans; this is how the deacons were chosen, and Stephen was one of the first deacons.
precepts.point: The high priest told him that there was such money laid up for the relief of widows and fatherless children, and that some of it belonged to Hircanus son of Tobias, a man of great dignity, and not as that wicked Simon had misinformed: in all four hundred talents of silver and two hundred of gold. And that it was altogether impossible that such wrong should be done unto them that had committed it to the holiness of the place.

note.label: From Brother To Betrayer

precepts.why:
The high priest Onias told Heliodorus “that there was such money laid up for the relief of widows and fatherless children.” The temple had money in it for the widows. So how come, in the days of the apostles, “there arose a murmuring of the Grecians against the Hebrews, because their widows were neglected in the daily ministration”? Why didn’t they just get it from the temple?

Because these were followers of Christ, and the priesthood had already agreed to cast out any man who confessed him. The widows of the disciples were getting nothing from the temple because they believed in Christ.

So the twelve said, “It is not reason that we should leave the word of God, and serve tables.” To serve tables means to take care of the widows, the orphans and all of that. “Wherefore, brethren, look ye out among you seven men of honest report, full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom, whom we may appoint over this business. But we will give ourselves continually to prayer, and to the ministry of the word.”

This is how the deacons were chosen. “And the saying pleased the whole multitude: and they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Ghost, and Philip, and Prochorus, and Nicanor, and Timon, and Parmenas, and Nicolas a proselyte of Antioch.” Stephen, the one we always read about, was one of the first deacons chosen. They set them before the apostles, “and when they had prayed, they laid their hands on them.”

So the care of widows and the fatherless has always been a sacred charge among our people, kept in the temple in Onias’s day and put into the deacons’ hands in the apostles’ day. That is what Simon betrayed to the Greeks.

The old substantiates the new. The gospel of Christ fulfills the prophecies written in the old testament, so to know who the Grecians are you go back to what was written aforetime. The scattered disciples went “preaching the word to none but unto the Jews only. And some of them were men of Cyprus and Cyrene, which, when they were come to Antioch, spake unto the Grecians, preaching the Lord Jesus.”

precepts.text: Certain Greeks came up to worship at the feast, and the disciples carried their request to Christ.
precepts.point: The feast of dedication Christ kept in John 10 commemorates the Maccabees driving out the Greeks and rededicating the temple the Greeks had profaned. Christ would not turn around a few months later and accept those same Greeks.

note.label: Acts 6: The Grecians Were Greek-Speaking Israelites

precepts.why:
“And there were certain Greeks among them that came up to worship at the feast”. They came up to worship at the passover, and the disciples carried their request to Christ.

Devout Israelites came back to Jerusalem to keep the feasts no matter where they were scattered, so these certain Greeks were Israelites keeping the law, not heathen. They are the same as the Grecians of Acts 6: Israelites out of the Greek provinces called by the name of the land. Christ answered them with prophecy; a real Greek got a very different answer.

This is why devout Israelites came to the feasts from every captivity, and why Greeks were at Jerusalem to worship at the passover. The law called all the males to appear, wherever they had been scattered, and the Grecians of Acts 6 were Israelites keeping that law.

Passover is the salvation of the righteous and the destruction of the enemies, the celebration of Israel's deliverance. It makes no sense that Christ would have the very Greeks who had just enslaved Israel keep a feast that commemorates their own destruction. The Greeks at the feast were Israelites.

Christ would not keep that feast and then turn around a few months later and accept those same Greeks at the passover. The Greeks who came to worship were Israelites.

That is the dedication of the sanctuary the feast of dedication in John 10 remembers, and it is why Christ, who kept that feast, was not accepting Greeks as his own a few months later. The Grecians of Acts 6 are Israelites, not the enemies Judas drove out.

precepts.text: The woman of Canaan cried, and Christ answered, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
precepts.point: Read logically, using comparison and context. Christianity teaches people to read the bible with a slave mind, taking a verse at face value the way the slave master intended, instead of going back to the beginning as you would with any book or film.

note.label: Acts 6: The Grecians Were Greek-Speaking Israelites

precepts.why:
When a real Greek came to Christ, the response was the opposite. “And, behold, a woman of Canaan came out of the same coasts, and cried unto him, saying, Have mercy on me, O Lord, thou Son of David”. She called him Son of David to disassociate her race from his.

“But he answered her not a word.” Christ ignored her, let the disciples say, “Send her away; for she crieth after us”, and then said plainly, “I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”

The Greeks of John 12 never had to go through that; Christ answered them with prophecy. The difference is that they were Israelites and she was not.

That same woman was a Greek, a Syrophenician by nation, and to her Christ said he was not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel. So when Greeks come up to worship at the feast and are answered with prophecy, and when Grecians murmur against the Hebrews in the church, those are not Greeks by nation; they are Israelites of the Greek captivity.

precepts.point: Paul sets the age at sixty because younger widows still have fleshly desires and will begin to wax wanton against Christ and want to marry, turning their focus off the work. A woman whose desire is toward the ministry and who has a pattern of good works is worthy to be taken care of; one still looking for a husband should marry and be provided for by a husband.

The daily ministration to the widows had a criterion. “Let not a widow be taken into the number under threescore years old, having been the wife of one man, Well reported of for good works; if she have brought up children, if she have lodged strangers, if she have washed the saints’ feet, if she have relieved the afflicted, if she have diligently followed every good work.”

The widow taken into the number must be sixty, the wife of one man, and well reported of for good works. “But the younger widows refuse: for when they have begun to wax wanton against Christ, they will marry; Having damnation, because they have cast off their first faith.” That is the order behind the ministration the Grecian widows were neglected in.

precepts.text: The chief priests, the elders, and all the council sought false witness against Christ to put Him to death.
precepts.point: The same thing was done to Paul in Acts 21, when they charged that he taught the people not to keep the customs of Moses.

note.label: Acts 6: The Grecians Were Greek-Speaking Israelites

precepts.why:
Unable to beat Stephen with the scriptures, they “suborned men”: bribed and induced them to give false testimony that he spoke “blasphemous words against Moses, and against God.” It is the same thing that was done to Christ. “Now the chief priests, and elders, and all the council, sought false witness against Jesus, to put him to death”. When the leaders cannot answer the word, they go looking for false witnesses.

Stephen was not teaching anyone to break the laws. He was teaching them to accept Christ as the sacrifice, and they could not tell the difference between mercy and keeping the law. So what was done to Christ was done to Stephen, and the same thing was done to Paul in Acts 21, when they charged that he taught the people not to keep the customs of Moses.

precepts.text: The council sought false witness against Christ, but the witnesses agreed not together, some saying they heard Him say He would destroy the temple.
precepts.point: It will come to a point where the words of the scripture themselves, harlot, sodomite, the law that a man should not lie with mankind, are treated as hate crimes, so a teacher must stay in the scriptures and not use his own words.

note.label: Acts 6: The Grecians Were Greek-Speaking Israelites

precepts.why:
They “set up false witnesses” who said Stephen “ceaseth not to speak blasphemous words against this holy place, and the law”, though he had not. It is the same pattern used against Christ: “the chief priests and all the council sought for witness against Jesus to put him to death; and found none.” “many bare false witness against him, but their witness agreed not together”, and certain rose up saying, “We heard him say, I will destroy this temple that is made with hands, and within three days I will build another made without hands.” False witnesses, and their stories did not even agree.

This is why we teach only the words of the bible. When they bring an accusation, we can answer that we spoke nothing but what is written in the same bible they swear on in court and read in their churches.

It will come to a point where the words of the scripture themselves, harlot, sodomite, the law that a man should not lie with mankind, are treated as hate crimes. So a teacher must stay in the scriptures and not use his own words.

precepts.point: Christ did only what the Most High intended, to make His soul an offering for sin. The scripture always shows that sacrifice was temporary and that obedience and mercy were desired above it.

The only thing set aside was the sacrifice and offerings, and even that is written throughout the old testament. Christ did only what the Most High intended, so the charge against Stephen was false.

points: People who do not know the history hear Grecians and assume the Most High began dealing with the heathen nations under Christ. But the Grecians here are Israelites scattered into the Greek provinces during the Greek captivity, the same way our people dropped off in England, the Caribbean, and the Americas take the name of the land that enslaved them and are called African American.

The old substantiates the new. The gospel of Christ fulfills the prophecies written in the old testament, and the apostles taught those Israelites scattered through the Assyrian, Babylonian, Persian, Greek, and Roman captivities. This is why the churches Paul wrote to sit in Greek provinces like Ephesus and Philippi.

Those who argue the Most High deals with the Greeks too are themselves so-called African American, West Indian, Haitian, and Jamaican, and they do not fit the title. To claim the grafting you must prove by your records which Gentile nation you are, and each Gentile nation had judgments that are not yet fulfilled.

Devout Israelites came back to Jerusalem to keep the feasts no matter where they were scattered, so the certain Greeks going up to worship at the passover in John 12 were Israelites keeping the law, not heathen.

Passover was the celebration of Israel's deliverance and the destruction of her enemies, and no stranger was to eat it. It makes no sense that Christ would have the very Greeks who had just enslaved Israel keep a feast that commemorates their own destruction.

The feast of dedication Christ kept in John 10 commemorates the Maccabees driving out the Greeks and rededicating the temple the Greeks had profaned. Christ would not turn around a few months later and accept those same Greeks.

When a real Greek came to Christ, the response was the opposite. The Syrophenician woman of Canaan cried, called Him Son of David to disassociate her race from His, and Christ ignored her, let the disciples say send her away, and then said plainly He was not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel. The Greeks of John 12 never had to do that; Christ answered them with prophecy.

Read logically, using comparison and context. Christianity teaches people to read the bible with a slave mind, taking a verse at face value the way the slave master intended, instead of going back to the beginning as you would with any book or film.

The reference works confirm it. The dictionaries say Greeks are generally of Hellenic race but the word may be used to indicate Jews, and that Grecians were Greek-speaking Jews, folk of the dispersion. The words generally and may show it is not always the heathen. Hellenist is defined as Jews who made Greek their tongue, and the Jewish synagogues dispersed through the cities of Greece and Egypt were called Hellenists.

The widows neglected in the daily ministration point to a set order of relief. There was a criterion: a widow taken into the number had to be threescore years old, the wife of one man, and well reported of for good works. This is not the Salvation Army handing everything out for free; people come in for their own benefit, so standards are in place.

Paul sets the age at sixty because younger widows still have fleshly desires and will begin to wax wanton against Christ and want to marry, turning their focus off the work. A woman whose desire is toward the ministry and who has a pattern of good works is worthy to be taken care of; one still looking for a husband should marry and be provided for by a husband.

To be full of the Holy Ghost is first and foremost to be keeping the laws. The office is desired by your works, your dedication, and your natural love for your people, not by gunning for a title. Moses was made a leader because he defended his people, and David showed the attributes of a leader wrestling lions and bears and facing Goliath before he was ever called.

These criteria are not for a title only. Everyone aiming for the kingdom must keep these laws, and any teacher giving oversight over the nation is an overseer who must fit them.
